{{short description|American mathematician}}
'''George Adam Pfeiffer''' (16 July 1889, New York City<ref>General Registry of the Members of the Phi Kappa Sigma Fraternity 1850–1920. Philadelphia, 1920; p. 448 [https://archive.org/stream/generalregistero00phik#page/448/mode/2up online]</ref> – 28 December 1943) was an American mathematician.

Pfeiffer received in 1910 his master's degree in engineering from [[Stevens Institute of Technology]] and then his A.M. in 1911 and in 1914 his Ph.D. in mathematics from [[Columbia University]]. He spent the academic year 1914–1915 as a Benjamin Pierce Instructor at Harvard University<ref>[https://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=njp.32101042319853;view=1up;seq=376 Pfeiffer appointed to Harvard U., Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society, 1914–1915, vol. 21, p. 368]</ref><ref>[https://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=njp.32101047634694;view=1up;seq=377 Pfeiffer's appointment to Princeton U., Bull. of the AMS, 1915–1916 vol. 22, p. 369]</ref> and then in 1915 became an instructor at [[Princeton University]].<ref>[https://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=mdp.39015066541049;view=1up;seq=28 The President's report. 1916, Princeton University]</ref> During WW I, he was in the U.S. army and at Princeton University taught meteorology to army aviation students. After the war he taught, starting as an instructor in February 1919,<ref name=ColumbiaUObit>{{cite news|title=Math Prof Passes Away After Illness|newspaper=Columbia Spectator|date=31 December 1943}}</ref> at Columbia University.<ref>[https://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=njp.32101047634728;view=1up;seq=292 Pfeifer's appointment to Columbia U., Bulletin of the AMS, 1918–1919, vol. 25, p. 284]</ref> There he became in 1924 an assistant professor and in 1931 an associate professor, in which position he remained until his death from a heart attack following minor surgery in 1943.<ref name=ColumbiaUObit/>

Pfeiffer is known for publishing the first example of a [[holomorphic function]] with a non-linearizable irrational indifferent fixed point.<ref>G. A. Pfeiffer: [https://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=njp.32101047634694;view=1up;seq=171 Existence of divergent solutions of the functional equations <math>\varphi[g(x)]=a\varphi(x),\ f[f(x)]=g(x)</math>, where <math>g(x)</math> is a given analytic function, in the irrational case]. Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society, vol. 22 (1916), p. 163</ref><ref>G. A. Pfeiffer: [https://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=mdp.39015024439120;view=1up;seq=199 On the Conformal Mapping of Curvilinear Angles. The Functional Equation <math>\varphi [ f(x) ] = a_1 \varphi (x)</math>]. Transactions of the American Mathematical Society, vol. 18 (1917), no. 2, pp. 185–198 {{mr|1501069}}</ref><ref>G. A. Pfeiffer: [https://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=mdp.39015024440250;view=1up;seq=23 The functional equation <math>f[f(x)]=g(x)</math>]. Annals of Mathematics (2nd series), vol. 20 (1918), pp. 13–22.</ref> The question of the linearizability of fixed points is of great importance in [[complex dynamics]]. After Pfeiffer's example, [[Hubert Cremer]] gave various criteria for the non-linearizability of irrational indifferent fixed points, while [[Carl Ludwig Siegel]] in 1942 gave conditions which imply the linearizability of such fixed points.<ref>A description and discussion of the results of Pfeiffer, Cremer and Siegel are available in the book by Alexander, Iavernaro and Rosa.</ref>

Pfeiffer was on the editorial staff of [[Annals of Mathematics]].
